method.label: Translate the roots and use coordinates

annotationRationale: The cyclic complex roots determine the regular octagon. A common-circumradius area bound proves the minimum, and coordinates supply the base and height for its value.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official solution's translation and coordinate base-height computation. Filled its minimum-area justification using shortest chords and the common-circumradius triangle area identity.

review.mathCheck: Translation gives eight roots on a circle of radius √3 at 45° intervals. The side satisfies s²=6−3√2 and the shortest diagonal is d=√6. Every vertex triangle has two sides at least s and another at least d, so K=abc/(4R)≥s²d/(4R). Consecutive vertices attain this, giving (3√2−3)/2, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of the first official solution 16 on page 9: translate, identify the octagon, and calculate base and height from coordinates. The added circumradius argument validly proves the minimum asserted by the official solution.
review.annotationCheck: The added minimum proof is adequately supported by the selected circumradius node. The explanation covers all vertex triples and is reconstructible at AMC 12 level.
